faq.question: What can I do with VoiceBridge?
faq.answer: Design your receptionist’s voice and greeting, organize conversations and contacts, manage appointments, curate business knowledge, and follow the next step from one clear workspace.

faq.question: Can the voice match my business?
faq.answer: Yes. Voice profiles, greetings, knowledge, and handoff preferences let you shape the character and context of your receptionist around your business.

faq.question: How do appointments stay connected to conversations?
faq.answer: A confirmed appointment keeps its conversation and contact together. You can move between related records, review the details, and manage changes from the workspace.

faq.question: What happens when a customer needs a person?
faq.answer: Define a clear handoff destination and give your team the context they need to continue the conversation. Human judgement stays part of the workflow.

faq.question: How should I choose a plan?
faq.answer: Start with your locations, call patterns, integrations, and team workflow. The plan comparison helps frame the conversation; pricing is tailored to the setup and usage you need.

companyStory.eyebrow: THE SPACE BETWEEN HELLO AND HANDLED
companyStory.title:
Small moments.
A bigger difference.
paragraphs: Someone calls with a question. A team member is out on a job. An appointment needs a little context. These are small moments, but they shape how a business feels.
VoiceBridge brings those moments into one considered experience. A recognizable voice. A clear next step. A workspace that makes the whole story easier to see.
The goal is simple: let technology take care of the in-between, so people can take care of what matters.

resources.title: The first ten seconds matter.
resources.summary: How to shape a greeting that sounds like your business — and makes the next question easy.
paragraphs: A useful greeting does three things: introduces the business, makes the customer feel welcome, and invites a clear next step. Keep it short enough that the caller can join the conversation.
Choose words your team would actually use. A warm, practical service business may sound different from a formal professional practice. Consistency matters more than sounding impressive.
Make the first question useful. Ask what the person needs before asking for details you may not need. This helps the conversation feel focused and respectful.
Write down the moments that should lead to a person. Complex, urgent, or sensitive requests deserve a clear route to human judgement. A good greeting is the beginning of that whole experience.

resources.title: Give every conversation a next step.
resources.summary: A practical way to connect context, appointments, and follow-up without losing the customer’s story.
paragraphs: Start by naming the outcome. Is the customer looking for an answer, an appointment, or a person? Keep these outcomes separate so the next action stays clear.
Capture just the details needed for that outcome. Confirm names, contact details, service, and appointment time before committing to the next step.
Keep the conversation linked to the contact and appointment. A team member should be able to understand what happened without reconstructing it from scattered notes.
Make failures visible and recoverable. A follow-up issue should not erase a confirmed appointment. Keep the original record and give your team a clear way to review what needs attention.

resources.title: Good answers start with clear knowledge.
resources.summary: What to include in your business guidance, and how to keep it understandable as you grow.
paragraphs: Use plain, specific language for the questions your team answers every day: services, coverage, opening hours, appointment expectations, and how to reach the right person.
Separate a general policy from a decision that needs judgement. Explain what can be answered directly and what should be passed to a team member.
Keep facts easy to maintain. Short, focused documents are easier to review than a single page containing every detail about your business.
Review knowledge when the business changes. A new service, a different schedule, or an updated policy should have a clear owner and a simple update process.
